reconciliation_amendments.rule: CHOCH = the first CLOSE beyond the most recent opposite swing, against the prior trend. Part 1's close through protected low in bullish trend and Part 2's close above last lower high after sweep are the same concept in opposite directions. BOS = close beyond prior swing in the trend's direction.
Part 1 Video 5 (sweep_fvg_entry) must also require a CHOCH/BOS close after the sweep. A sweep alone is not enough. Not every wick is a sweep. Let structure confirm it.
Part 1 Video 6 required 2 consecutive closes. Part 2 adds close beyond + retest & hold. Both forms confirm that price stays outside the level.
A TRAP (wick through, close back inside) followed by CHOCH provides valid reversal context. Entry requires a zone (FVG/OB in discount or premium).
The 50% midpoint is a watch level where price often reacts; classification of setup validity is decided by candle close.

Replaces single-fractal swings with ranked swings: STH/STL (n=1), ITH/ITL (higher STH), LTH/LTL (higher ITH). Requires confirmation lag; zero repainting. Protected swing anchored to intermediate rank.
Sweep setups use the sweep extreme as stop loss. OB setups use below the block. If both apply, the sweep extreme takes precedence as the wider structural invalidation.

reconciliation_amendments.topic: Target logic via Range Liquidity Loop
reconciliation_amendments.rule: Target next liquidity pool: first unmitigated internal range liquidity (IRL gap) if one sits between price and far pool and R:R passes; otherwise external pool (ERL: EQH/EQL, PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL).
Higher-timeframe pools first (PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL), then lower-timeframe reaction. Liquidity first, then structure, then the zone, in that order.
An OB candidate strictly requires BOTH a structure break (BOS) AND an unmitigated FVG left on the impulse. No break, no gap = just a candle.
Position size = risk_amount / (stop_distance * value_per_unit). Never derived from available margin or leverage.
Futures on central exchange has real traded volume; spot forex has no central exchange and MT5 volume is broker tick volume. Forbid algorithms assuming real volume in forex.

BOS.name: Break of Structure
BOS.definition: A candle CLOSES beyond the previous swing high (bullish) or swing low (bearish) in the direction of the trend.

CHOCH.name: Change of Character
CHOCH.definition: The first candle CLOSE beyond the most recent opposite swing against the prior trend (e.g. close through protected low in uptrend or close above lower high after sweep).

Protected Swing.name: Protected Low (Bullish) / Protected High (Bearish)
Protected Swing.definition: The swing that started the move that broke structure. Selected from intermediate-term swings. While it holds, structure is intact.

BSL_SSL.name: Buy-Side Liquidity (BSL) / Sell-Side Liquidity (SSL)
BSL_SSL.definition: Resting buy stops and breakout orders above old highs (BSL); resting sell stops and breakout orders below old lows (SSL). Pools are a map, not a promise.

Sweep.name: Liquidity Sweep
Sweep.definition: A wick penetration through a liquidity level followed by a candle close back inside the prior range.

FVG.name: Fair Value Gap / Imbalance
FVG.definition: Three-candle price imbalance where candle 1 wick and candle 3 wick do not overlap. Midpoint (50%) is equilibrium. Invalidated on candle close through gap.

Order Block.name: Order Block (OB)
Order Block.definition: The last opposite-colour candle before a strong move that breaks structure AND leaves an FVG. Zone = high to low.

IFVG.name: Inversion Fair Value Gap
IFVG.definition: A broken FVG that flips role on return: old support becomes resistance (bearish inversion) or old resistance becomes support.

Premium Discount.name: Premium / Discount Equilibrium
Premium Discount.definition: Dividing the swing range in half (50% equilibrium). Buy in discount, sell in premium. Range invalid on close beyond swing extreme.

ERL_IRL.name: External vs Internal Range Liquidity
ERL_IRL.definition: ERL = stops outside range (EQH/EQL, PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL). IRL = FVGs and minor swings inside range. Price tends to loop from ERL to IRL, then IRL to ERL.

Swing Hierarchy.name: Swing Hierarchy (STH/ITH/LTH)
Swing Hierarchy.definition: Rank 1 STH/STL (n=1 each side). Rank 2 ITH/ITL (lower STHs each side). Rank 3 LTH/LTL (lower ITHs each side). Confirmed-only; no repainting.

Five Check Model.name: Five-Check Master Model (Setup A)
Five Check Model.definition: 1. Sweep -> 2. Structure (CHOCH) -> 3. Range (Discount) -> 4. Entry (FVG+OB) -> 5. Plan (SL below sweep, TP at equal highs). All 5 or no trade.

cards.title: Inducement + Order Block Entry
cards.claim: The first pullback after a push looks like the perfect buy but is bait; stops sit under it, big buyers need those sell orders to fill, so price drops, takes the stops, and taps the order block.
rules: Do not buy the first pullback (inducement) [VIDEO 1]
Wait for sweep of the pullback low, then a bullish close in the block. That close is the entry [VIDEO 1]
Stop below the block. Target the highs [VIDEO 1]
A close below the block means the setup is off [VIDEO 1]
Order block must be qualified with BOS and FVG [ART-09]
cards.coach_lesson: That pullback wasn't your entry. It was bait.

cards.title: Premium / Discount Location Filter
cards.claim: Take the last move up from the protected low to the high, cut it in half. Top half = premium, bottom half = discount. In an uptrend buy in discount, not just anywhere.
rules: In an uptrend buy in discount (<= 50% equilibrium). In a downtrend sell in premium (>= 50% equilibrium) [VIDEO 2]
A missed trade costs nothing; price may never come down that far [VIDEO 2]
If price closes below the swing low, structure is broken and range is invalid [ART-07]
cards.coach_lesson: Two traders, same trend, same stop, same target. Where they bought decides the quality.

cards.title: Protected Low Marker
cards.claim: Many swing lows exist; most are noise. The one that counts: the low that started the move that broke the last high. While it holds, buyers are in control.
rules: Do not mark every fractal. Mark the low that broke something (caused BOS with body close) [VIDEO 3]
Anchor to intermediate-term swing rank from swing hierarchy [ART-02, DERIVED]
Small pauses inside a move can break without changing trend structure [VIDEO 3]
cards.coach_lesson: Mark the low that broke something.

cards.title: Trend by Structure
cards.claim: Trend is structure, not the last candle. Higher highs + higher lows = uptrend. A hard drop that stops above the last higher low changes nothing. Only a candle close below that low puts the uptrend in trouble.
rules: Trend = BULL while HH/HL structure intact and no body close below protected low [VIDEO 4]
Trend = BEAR mirror for lower highs and lower lows [VIDEO 4]
Closes only decide; wicks do not break trend [VIDEO 4, ART-10]
cards.coach_lesson: Don't judge the trend by the last candle. Judge it by the last low.

cards.title: Liquidity Sweep + FVG Entry
cards.claim: Price breaks obvious lows, but it was a sweep, not a breakdown: stops taken, big buyer filled, price snaps back, candle leaves an FVG. When price returns, if the gap holds, that is the entry.
rules: Sweep = wick beyond level, candle closes back inside [VIDEO 5, ART-10]
A sweep alone is not enough: price must break structure (CHOCH) after the sweep [ART-06, ART-10]
Entry in the gap. Stop below the sweep low. Target the highs above [VIDEO 5, ART-06]
If price closes through the gap, setup is off [VIDEO 5, 10, ART-08]
cards.coach_lesson: The sweep shows who stepped in, the gap shows where to join them.

cards.title: Breakout vs Trap Classifier
cards.claim: Price runs above the high. While candle is forming you cannot know. Trap: falls straight back inside. Breakout: close above AND stays outside.
rules: A trap comes back inside. A breakout stays outside [VIDEO 6]
Breakout confirmed by either: 2 consecutive closes beyond OR close beyond + retest & hold [VIDEO 6, ART-10]
A trap plus a CHOCH provides valid reversal context [ART-10, ART-06]
cards.coach_lesson: A trap comes back inside. A breakout stays outside.

cards.title: Liquidity Map
cards.claim: Obvious highs and equal highs attract stops. A large player needs counterparties, so price pushes into them, orders trigger, player fills, price snaps back.
rules: Liquidity is not a signal. It tells you where to watch, not what to do [VIDEO 7]
Map EQH/EQL, PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL for watchlists and target selection [VIDEO 7, ART-04]
Never enter a trade on raw liquidity touch alone [VIDEO 7, ART-06]
cards.coach_lesson: Liquidity is not a signal. It tells you where to watch, not what to do.

cards.title: Failed FVG / Inversion
cards.claim: A close through an FVG does not kill it; price often returns from the other side. Old support becomes resistance.
rules: Close through gap flips role (inversion) [VIDEO 8]
Confirmation candle dropping away validates inverted gap holding as resistance [VIDEO 8]
Stop above far edge of gap; target next opposing liquidity [ASSUMPTION, ART-03]
cards.coach_lesson: Same zone, same return. The close decides. A failed FVG isn't finished, it just changed sides.

cards.title: FVG Quality Score
cards.claim: A gap is only as good as the move that made it. Strong when it broke previous high with body close; weak inside choppy range.
rules: Strong gap: formed in the move that caused a BOS with body close (+2) [VIDEO 9, ART-08]
Weak gap: formed inside range with nothing broken (+0; reject by default) [VIDEO 9]
Penalty if unswept liquidity rests immediately below a bullish gap (-1/-2) [VIDEO 9]
cards.coach_lesson: A gap is only as good as the move that made it.

cards.title: FVG Return and Close
cards.claim: Depth is not the signal; watch the close. Bullish held: candle wicks into gap but closes back above 50%. Broken: close through gap.
rules: Classification: TAP, HELD (close above 50% midpoint), CONFIRMED (pushes away), BROKEN (close through) [VIDEO 10, ART-08]
Broken gap cancels setup immediately [VIDEO 10, ART-08]
cards.coach_lesson: Don't ask if price returned. Ask how it closed.

cards.title: Why FVGs Get Revisited
cards.claim: An FVG is an imbalance from fast one-sided delivery. Price does not have to come back; an FVG is not a magnet. Context tells you if return matters.
rules: An FVG is not a magnet. Never assume FVGs always fill [VIDEO 11]
Never place standing limit orders based purely on FVG presence [VIDEO 11]
Only trade returns when accompanied by sweep and structure context [VIDEO 11, ART-06]
cards.coach_lesson: An FVG is not a magnet. Price does not have to come back. Context tells you if the return really matters.

cards.title: Break-Even Too Early
cards.claim: Moving stop to BE too early stops out winning trades on normal pullbacks. Price does not know where you entered. Move stop when market gives a reason.
rules: Remove fixed +1R / +0.5R break-even rules [VIDEO 12]
Stop trails only when a new structural level forms that invalidates setup if broken (e.g. new protected low above entry after confirmed BOS) [VIDEO 12, DERIVED]
Default be_move_mode = structure_only [VIDEO 12]
cards.coach_lesson: Move your stop when the market gives you a reason, not just because you're finally in profit.

cards.title: Middle of the Range Filter
cards.claim: In the middle of a range price is far from both edges, with room against you either way, no clear advantage. Sometimes best location is somewhere else.
rules: Detect ranges with >= 2 touches at support and resistance [VIDEO 13]
If price is in middle 40%-60% band, output NO_TRADE_MIDDLE [VIDEO 13, ASSUMPTION]
Trade only near range edges with clear invalidation [VIDEO 13]
cards.coach_lesson: Don't force a decision. Movement is not location. Sometimes the best location is somewhere else.

cards.title: Right Direction, Bad Entry
cards.claim: Entering late after extension expands risk and shrinks room to target. Right direction, bad entry. Don't chase the move; wait for new setup or let it go.
rules: Compute risk and room from live fill price [VIDEO 14]
Reject if live R:R < min_rr (default 1.5) [VIDEO 14, ASSUMPTION]
Reject if entry price is extended > max_extension (default 1.0x risk) beyond setup level [VIDEO 14, ASSUMPTION]
Never widen the stop loss to force R:R [VIDEO 14]
cards.coach_lesson: Right direction, bad entry. Don't chase the move; wait for a new setup or let it go.

cards.title: Weakening Pushes & Momentum Decay
cards.claim: New HH != strong trend. When moves get smaller this usually means trend may end or enter big correction. Caution flag, not a reversal trigger.
rules: Measure consecutive impulse leg lengths [VIDEO 15]
If last 2-3 legs shrink, flag momentum = DECAYING [VIDEO 15]
Reduce position size or block continuation entries [VIDEO 15, DERIVED]
Do not flip trend until confirmed CHOCH [VIDEO 15, VIDEO 4]
cards.coach_lesson: New HH != strong trend. Weakening pushes warn that the trend may end.

cards.title: IPDA Lens: Price Seeks Liquidity or Rebalances (ICT 01)
cards.claim: Price is not wandering; it is delivered from one level to the next. Every move either seeks liquidity (stops outside range) or rebalances (fills FVG inside range).
rules: Classify market state into SEEKING_LIQUIDITY or REBALANCING [ART-05]
Lens only; not a mechanical trade rule [ART-05]
Caveat: nobody outside can prove an algorithm exists. The coach must never present IPDA as established fact [ART-05]
cards.coach_lesson: Ask what price is reaching for.

cards.title: Buy-Side / Sell-Side Liquidity (ICT 02)
cards.claim: Stops rest above old highs (BSL) and below old lows (SSL). Cleanest pools: EQH/EQL, PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL. Higher timeframe = more orders.
rules: Map pools: EQH, EQL, PDH, PDL, PWH, PWL, ranked swings [ART-04]
Weight: PWH/PWL > PDH/PDL > EQH/EQL > minor swings [ART-04, ASSUMPTION]
Two outcomes when price reaches pool: sweep (wick and snaps back) or run (continues) [ART-04]
Caveat: nobody can see the stops; pools are a map of where orders probably rest, not a promise [ART-04]
cards.coach_lesson: Nobody can see the stops. Pools are a map of where orders probably rest, not a promise.

cards.title: External vs Internal Range Liquidity Loop (ICT 03)
cards.claim: From external liquidity, price tends to draw back to internal; from internal, it draws to external. Gap is often the next draw before far high.
rules: ERL = liquidity outside range (EQH/EQL, PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL) [ART-03]
IRL = fair value gaps and minor swings inside range [ART-03]
Loop: sweep ERL -> draw to IRL gap -> rebalance -> reach for opposing ERL [ART-03]
Caveat: a tendency, not a law. Sometimes price skips the gap, sometimes trades straight through [ART-03]
cards.coach_lesson: From external to internal, from internal to external. A tendency, not a law.

cards.title: Swing Hierarchy: STH / ITH / LTH (ICT 05)
cards.claim: Short-term high (STH): candle with lower high on each side (n=1). Intermediate-term high (ITH): STH with lower STH on each side. Long-term high (LTH): ITH with lower ITH on each side.
rules: Recursive 3-tier swing ranking [ART-02]
Confirmation lag: each rank needs the next swing to confirm it (the bigger the high, the later you know) [ART-02]
Zero repainting: swings confirmed only after confirmation candle closes [ART-02]
STH for LTF entries; ITH for structure/BOS/CHOCH; LTH for HTF targets and bias [ART-02, ASSUMPTION]
cards.coach_lesson: Most highs and lows don't matter. The bigger the high, the later you know.

cards.title: Four Phases of a Move (ICT 07)
cards.claim: 1 Consolidation -> 2 Expansion -> 3 Retracement -> 4 Reversal -> new range, loop repeats.
rules: Classify current market phase using confirmed swings [ART-01]
Descriptive and lagging only; never use phase as a standalone entry/exit trigger [ART-01]
Caveat: easy to label afterward; live, a pullback and a reversal can look the same [ART-01]
cards.coach_lesson: Easy to label afterward. Live, a pullback and a reversal look the same.

cards.title: Five-Check Trade Plan (Master Template)
cards.claim: 1. Sweep equal lows -> 2. Break structure (CHOCH) -> 3. Range in discount -> 4. Entry in FVG with OB right under it -> 5. Plan before price arrives (stop below sweep, target equal highs). All five or no trade.
rules: Check 1: Sweep of liquidity (wick through, close back inside) [ART-06]
Check 2: Structure break (CHOCH body close above last lower high) [ART-06]
Check 3: Equilibrium: entry strictly in discount (< 50% of sweep-to-high leg) [ART-06]
Check 4: Confluence of FVG and Order Block in discount [ART-06]
Check 5: Plan: entry in gap, stop below sweep low, target equal highs, R:R >= 2.0 [ART-06, ASSUMPTION]
All five or no trade. No sweep, no break, no discount -> wait for next setup [ART-06]
cards.coach_lesson: Sweep. Break. Range. Entry. Plan. Five checks, one trade.

cards.title: Premium / Discount / Equilibrium (Amends V2)
cards.claim: Draw range from swing low to swing high; 50% is equilibrium. In an uptrend buyers want discount; same stop, much better trade. If price closes below swing low, range is invalid.
rules: 50% equilibrium split of swing range [ART-07]
A gap in premium gets run through; a gap in discount holds and turns [ART-07]
Range invalidation: close below swing low breaks structure and invalidates discount [ART-07]
cards.coach_lesson: Same pattern, better location. If structure breaks, discount wasn't cheap after all.

cards.title: Fair Value Gap Definition
cards.claim: Three candles: high of candle 1 and low of candle 3 do not overlap. Middle candle left prices behind. Often price reaches 50% midpoint and turns. Invalid on close through gap.
rules: Bullish FVG: high[c1] < low[c3], zone = [high[c1], low[c3]] [ART-08]
Bearish FVG: low[c1] > high[c3], zone = [high[c3], low[c1]] [ART-08]
Track 50% midpoint level as key watch line [ART-08]
Context decides: strong when liquidity taken first and causes BOS; weak inside range [ART-08]
Invalidation: closed candle through gap cancels setup [ART-08]
cards.coach_lesson: Not every gap matters. Context decides.

cards.title: Order Block Qualification (Amends V1)
cards.claim: The last opposite candle before a strong move that breaks structure. Qualification: must break structure AND leave an FVG. Sequence: sweep -> CHOCH -> pullback into OB.
rules: Bullish OB = last down candle before strong up move; Bearish OB = last up candle before strong down move [ART-09]
Qualification: MUST break structure AND leave an FVG. No break, no gap = just a candle [ART-09]
Order of analysis: liquidity first, then structure, then zone [ART-09]
Invalidation: close through the order block cancels setup [ART-09]
cards.coach_lesson: No break, no gap = just a candle. Liquidity first, then structure, then the zone.

cards.title: Liquidity Sweep vs Breakout (Amends V6)
cards.claim: Sweep = wick through level, close back inside. Breakout = close above, retest, hold. A sweep of yesterday's high carries more weight than a 1-minute wick. Wick extreme is the risk line.
rules: Sweep requires wick beyond level + close inside [ART-10]
Sweep requires subsequent CHOCH to become tradable [ART-10]
Breakout requires either 2 closes beyond OR close beyond + retest & hold [ART-10]
Risk line: stop placed beyond wick extreme. Close beyond extreme invalidates [ART-10]
cards.coach_lesson: Liquidity shows where price may go; structure shows what it did there.

cards.title: Price Action Primer & S/R Zones
cards.claim: Body = who won; wicks = where price was pushed back. Support/resistance are zones, not lines. Price action doesn't predict, it shows you where you're wrong.
rules: Candle anatomy: compute body and wick ratios for rejection verification [ART-11]
Support and resistance treated as zones with ATR-based width (~0.5x ATR) [ART-11, ASSUMPTION]
Mandatory rule: define invalidation level BEFORE placing any order [ART-11]
cards.coach_lesson: Price action doesn't predict the future. It shows you where you're wrong.

cards.title: Futures Contracts & Leverage Mechanics
cards.claim: Futures traded on central exchange (CME, CBOT, NYMEX, COMEX). Clearinghouse guarantees trades. Margin is a deposit; gains/losses settle daily. Size from stop, not margin.
rules: Size your trade from your stop, never from your margin [ART-12]
Position size = risk_amount / (stop_distance * value_per_unit) [ART-12]
Time-sensitive caveat: E-mini S&P ~$390k contract value changes with index level; check current values [ART-12]
cards.coach_lesson: The contract is simple. The leverage is not. Size your trade from your stop, not from your margin.

cards.title: Futures vs Forex & Bot Data Cautions
cards.claim: Futures = central exchange, real volume, fixed contracts. Forex = decentralized broker, tick volume, flexible lots, spread/swap. Different markets, same edge.
rules: MT5 forex volume is broker tick volume, not real traded volume; do not assume real volume [ART-13]
Account for spread and rollover swap in execution modeling [ART-13]
Region-specific caveat: tax rules (US 60/40) and leverage caps (50:1 US, 30:1 UK/EU) are region-dependent [ART-13]
cards.coach_lesson: Different markets. Same edge. In forex, volume is broker tick volume.

pedagogical_rules: Always teach from the 28 verified video cards using the Coach Lesson lines as anchors.
Explain the underlying institutional mechanics (liquidity pools, stop clusters, order imbalance) rather than just chart patterns.
Always state prominently: educational only, not financial advice, trading involves risk of loss, no profit guarantees.

Mandatory caveat phrases: 'a tendency, not a law', 'nobody can see the stops', 'nobody outside can prove an algorithm exists', 'easy to label afterward', 'price action doesn't predict, it shows where you're wrong'.

Never claim: FVGs always fill; every new high means a strong trend; move to break even once in profit; liquidity sweeps are entry signals on their own; IPDA is proven fact; forex volume is real volume.
When evaluating a setup, walk sequentially through H0, G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, G6 and identify the exact gate that fails.
Mark time-sensitive or region-specific figures (E-mini value, leverage caps, 60/40 tax) as illustrative; instruct user to check current values and local regulations.
Do not teach ICT 04, 06, or 08 topics beyond what appears in verified cards; state clearly that they were announced but not uploaded.
Enforce that position size derives strictly from stop distance, never from margin or leverage.
All trading decisions require completed, closed candles. Never judge or enter on a still-forming bar.
